topology_reasoning.mechanism: A broad center core narrows into an inverse-taper tip while two side cores begin as narrow tips, widen through a long taper, and gently fan outward into separate output rails. The black regions are the three material cores; the white gaps are intentional and no raw connecting polygon is present.

observed_geometry.center_core: starts at the left footprint edge, is nearly horizontal, and tapers from about 0.270 um to about 0.075 um by x about 25.05 um
observed_geometry.side_cores: begin around x=3.04 um at center offsets about +0.265 and -0.275 um, taper from about 0.072 um to about 0.244 um, then fan to output center offsets about +0.731 and -0.728 um
observed_geometry.output_section: upper and lower rails are nearly horizontal and full width from approximately x=36 um to the right footprint edge

topology_reasoning.parametric_interpretation: The center taper length, side taper length, tip widths, side-to-center gaps, fan-out, and bend radius control modal evolution and coupling; delta_length is the physical straight output-lead/transfer section and is the knob used for the required geometry-response proof.

iterations.change_made: Initial three-path primitive model: constant-width sampled center inverse taper plus two variable-width smooth side rails; initial output lead used delta_length.
Corrected the side output lead to reach x=40.0 um, sampled the center taper with 128 path points, made side_gap live, and delayed/smoothed the fanout control points.
Reduced center and side widths by the measured one-pixel excess and replaced the coarse fanout with target-derived sigmoid control points and a smaller Euler rounding radius.
Added the measured upper/lower taper centerline slopes and lower-rail asymmetry; flattened the assembled cell and disabled GDS metadata so the area proof sees top-level layer polygons.
